items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: So Howard kind of reset my mind, and then I was also able to join his group at that time it was called Substructure.

ctx.x: Yeah most definitely. So again, like mentors and stuff, people that you run into that change your life and change your course in history. So in New York City like I said, I grew up on the Latin, you know, New York scene, on the lower east side, which was a big Latin mecca. So I was playing — I had a valve trombone that I was doing gigs on on the Latin scene, playing valve trombones. And during the weekend the Latin scene, you can do a gig, an early gig starting around maybe eight, then you move to another venue…

So he came in and he just like shattered my thoughts of what a tuba can do in a improvisational setting, or a setting where the music is not written down or structured and everything. Where I’m not playing a tuba part but I’m actually doing what the saxophones and everybody else is doing. I’m given the freedom to improvise and do all types of things. items.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: Before I forget, a mutual acquaintance told me to ask you about “Madame Butterfly.”

ctx.x: And even so, things like “One O’clock Jump” and that sort of thing, they made that up on the bandstand and when it was in good enough shape they recorded it. But all those guys contributed to it.
Before I forget, a mutual acquaintance told me to ask you about “Madame Butterfly.”
